paras.text: … because here investment is more than saving. For example, at the standard O-N of income, investment is N-P while saving is N-R. Its meaning is that as much money as people save, more than that is spent on investment, i.e. as many goods are produced, the demand for them will be more than that. Business people will feel that the prices of goods are increasing and their profit is becoming more; thus they will increase their production. Labourers will get employment, national income will begin to increase, until it becomes O-H again. As it were, it is proved that national income always settles at that standard where saving and investment are equal to each other.

Its meaning is that as much money as people save, more than that is spent on investment, i.e. as many goods are produced, the demand for them will be more than that. 5. Functional Relation Between Income and Consumption

Between income and consumption of wealth a functional relation (Functional Relation) is found. If income is called Y, consumption of wealth C and the functional relation F, then the equation becomes thus:

$C = F(Y)$

It is read thus: “Consumption is a Function of Income”, i.e. consumption is a function of income. To understand this mutual relation of income and consumption of wealth we should keep two concepts in mind.

1. Average propensity to consume (APC)

“Propensity to consume means the mutual ratio of consumption and income in a particular period”, i.e. that ratio according to which a person consumes some part of his monthly income. For example, if someone’s monthly income is three hundred rupees and expenditure two hundred and seventy rupees, then the propensity to consume will be this. “The mutual ratio of consumption and income is called the average propensity to consume.”

له دې مراد دا دی چې د عاید په زیاتېدو په سپما کې څومره زیاتوالی راځي. د بېلګې په توګه که د یوه کس میاشتنی عاید له یو زر روپیو یو نیم زر روپیو ته ورسېږي او د دوه سوه روپیو پر ځای څلور سوه روپۍ وسپموي، نو حاشیوي سپما به دا وي. "د سپما د بدلون او د عاید د بدلون دوه اړخیزې نسبت ته د سپما حاشیوي تمایل ویل کېږي."

$MPS = \frac{\text{change in saving}}{\text{change in income}} = \frac{200}{500} = 0.4$

APC + APS = 1

MPC + MPS = 1

6. د ملي عاید ټاکونکي (یا اغېزمنوونکي) عوامل (Factors or Determinants of National Income)

د یوه هېواد د خلکو سوکالي په دې پورې اړه لري چې هلته ملي عاید لوړ وي. نو اوس دا پوښتنه پیدا کېږي چې د یوه هېواد ملي عاید په کومو عواملو او چارو پورې اړه لري؟ په بل عبارت، کوم عوامل په ملي عاید اغېز (Influence) کوي؟ ځینې یې دا دي:

Therefore when his income increased, there remained no room for much increase in his expenditure. As income keeps increasing, the proportion of expenditure keeps decreasing; as it were, the additional expenditure out of additional income, i.e. the marginal propensity to consume, keeps decreasing. By marginal propensity to consume is meant: “The mutual ratio of change in consumption and change in income is called the marginal propensity to consume.” Its measurement is thus:

$MPC = \frac{\Delta C}{\Delta Y} = \frac{\text{change in expenditure}}{\text{change in income}} = \frac{80}{100} = 0.8$

3. Average propensity to save

By it is meant how much amount is saved out of income, or what is the ratio (Ratio) of saving? For example, a person’s monthly income is one thousand rupees and he saves two hundred rupees out of it; then the propensity to save will be this. “The mutual ratio of saving and income is called the average propensity to save.” 200/1000, i.e. 0.2. As it were, the equation will be thus:

$APS = \frac{S}{Y} = \frac{\text{Saving}}{\text{Income}}$

4. Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS)

By it is meant how much increase occurs in saving by the increase of income. For example, if a person’s monthly income increases from one thousand rupees to one thousand five hundred rupees and he begins to save four hundred rupees instead of two hundred rupees out of it, then the marginal saving will be this. “The mutual ratio of change in saving and change in income is called the marginal propensity to save.”

$MPS = \frac{\text{change in saving}}{\text{change in income}} = \frac{200}{500} = 0.4$

APC + APS = 1

MPC + MPS = 1
